facts.statement: Project Gigabit includes a £5 billion commitment for hardest-to-reach areas.
BDUK funds contracts for gigabit-capable wholesale infrastructure.
The procurement approach succeeds the Superfast programme.
Potential intervention areas exclude commercially viable build.
Potential intervention areas exclude infrastructure planned within three years.
BDUK also requests plans beyond three years when available.
National premises-level returns have been requested since January 2022.
Suppliers submit on a four-monthly cycle.
The return months are January, May and September.
NR OMR seeks the latest existing-build information.
NR OMR seeks the latest planned-build information.
Supplier submissions inform Project Gigabit eligibility.
Commercial-plan credibility is assessed before subsidy targeting.
Public Review validation follows OMR assessment.
Eligible premises are grouped into intervention areas.
BDUK combines supplier data with Ofcom Connected Nations.
OMR assesses wholesale broadband infrastructure, not leased lines.
Supporting evidence packs accompany supplier submissions.
Outputs are intended for GOV.UK publication.
Suppliers are asked to refresh national data every four months.
